mainTopic: Who is included in ערכין and דמים, the unspecified ערך, pledging limbs, and whether a vital part is judged as the whole (נידון בכבודו).
overview: This amud works through a ברייתא on the פסוקים of ערכין in ויקרא 27. The word נפשות teaches that a woman can make a ערך vow and that a מנוול or a מוכה שחין can be valuated. The words והיה ערכך teach that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can be pledged by דמים (market value), but they have no ערך, since only a definite male or female has one. The גמרא then explains ערך סתום: someone who pledges an unnamed ערך pays the smallest amount, three שקלים, because of תפשת מרובה לא תפשת. רב נחמן gives two opposite versions of whether this amount can be lowered for a poor person (הֶשֵּׂג יָד). Next the גמרא learns that a ערך covers a whole person, not a limb. A part that life depends on counts as the whole person, while the dead and the dying are left out. It then shows how one word can teach several lessons. Finally, רבא says a טומטום is נידון בכבודו, and אביי challenges him from the case of the head of a slave, donkey or cow. They settle it by splitting קדשי מזבח from קדשי בדק הבית, and a new challenge about the cow begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about a woman who makes a valuation vow?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the פסוק speaks about a man who valuates, and asks where we learn that a woman can valuate too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only know about a man who valuates someone, whether a man or a woman. Where do we learn about a woman who valuates a man, or a woman who valuates a woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that the פסוק says 'a man' who vows. It asks how we know that a woman making the vow is also included. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person being valuated can clearly be a man or a woman, because the Torah lists values for both. The open question is about the person making the vow. The wording 'איש' seems to limit that to men.

steps.title: Another use of 'persons': a repulsive person and one with boils

steps.title: Why we needed a פסוק to include them
steps.stepSummary: Without נפשות, we might have linked ערכין to דמים. Then people with no market value would be excluded from ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought, since it says 'a vow according to your valuation': anyone who is part of market-value pledges is part of ערכין, and anyone who is not part of market-value pledges is not part of ערכין. So the פסוק says 'persons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the inclusion in step 3 was needed. Without it, we might have tied ערכין to דמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נדר בערכך' put 'vow' and 'valuation' side by side. That could suggest that only someone who has a market price can be valuated. A מנוול and a מוכה שחין have no market value, so they would have been left out. נפשות teaches that anyone who is a living person can be valuated, whatever his market price.

keyTerms.meaning: For one might have thought; it introduces a mistaken assumption

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערכין and דמים. ערכין is a fixed amount from the Torah, based only on age and gender. דמים is whatever the person is worth on the market. The whole ברייתא is about these two being separate.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ערכין does not depend on how much a person is worth on the market.

steps.title: 'Your valuation shall be' includes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס for דמים

steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a new inclusion from a different phrase. Someone who pledges the market value of a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס must pay it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of step 3. There, people without market value were included in ערכין. Here, people who are not part of ערכין are included in דמים.

steps.title: Why we needed a פסוק for this inclusion
steps.stepSummary: Without והיה ערכך, we might have thought that only someone who is part of ערכין can be part of דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought, since it says 'a vow according to your valuation': anyone who is part of ערכין is part of market-value pledges, and anyone who is not part of ערכין is not part of market-value pledges. So the פסוק says 'Then your valuation shall be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the inclusion in step 5 was needed. It uses the same 'one might have thought' reasoning as step 4, but in the reverse direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking 'vow' and 'valuation' could also suggest that דמים depends on ערכין. Since a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not part of ערכין, they would have been left out of דמים. The extra phrase והיה ערכך cuts that link, so they are still included in דמים.
steps.whatToRemember: ערכין and דמים are two separate systems. A מנוול and a מוכה שחין have ערכין even without market value, and a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס have דמים even though they are not part of ערכין.

steps.title: The word 'the male' excludes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word הזכר that only a real male gets a man's valuation. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The male': this means a male, and not a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the word הזכר ('the male') closely. It uses it to exclude a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס from the valuation of a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 included them in דמים, which is pledging someone's market value. Now we learn the other side: they are left out of ערכין, the fixed amounts the תורה sets. The added 'ה' in הזכר limits the law to a clear, definite male.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose gender cannot be seen, because the body is covered
A person with both male and female features
'The male', a word in the פסוק about ערכין

phrases.english: "The male" means a male,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's treatment of טומטום and אנדרוגינוס. They are included in דמים but excluded from ערכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס cannot be valued at a man's ערך.

steps.title: Maybe they should get a woman's valuation instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possibility: maybe a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are only kept out of a man's valuation, but still get a woman's.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they are not valued like a man, but they are valued like a woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a possible mistake a person could make. This sets up the next step, which will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הזכר only excludes them from the male amounts. So someone could think they fall back to the lower female amounts. The ברייתא raises this so it can rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think', which opens a mistaken idea the ברייתא will reject
The fixed valuation for a man or for a woman

phrases.english: One might think they are not included in the valuation of a man,
but they are included in the valuation of a woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a gap left by step 7. Being excluded from the male amount might still leave the female amount.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס get the female valuation, since they were only excluded from the male one?

steps.title: Only a definite male or a definite female
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names a male and a female, which teaches that only a definitely male or definitely female person has a ערך. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are fully left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Your valuation shall be for the male... and if it is a female.' This means a definite male and a definite female, and not a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 8. The פסוק uses clear male and clear female categories, so a person of uncertain gender fits neither.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the male and female parts of the פסוק together shows that each one needs certainty. Since a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not definitely female, they don't get a woman's ערך either. They are fully outside ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', which brings a פסוק as the answer
Definite, certain (the male and the female form)

steps.whatToRemember: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are included in דמים (market value) but are completely outside ערכין, since only a definite male or a definite female has a ערך.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Then your valuation shall be for the male...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:3–4

phrases.english: and if it is a female"
a definite male, a definite female,
and not a tumtum or an androginos.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires a definite male or a definite female, so they get no ערך at all.

steps.title: What is an 'unspecified valuation'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to an earlier line of the ברייתא: בערכך includes an ערך סתום. It asks what that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'According to your valuation' comes to include an unspecified valuation. What is an unspecified valuation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes an earlier part of the ברייתא and asks what one of its terms means. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic within the same ברייתא. The word בערכך was said to include something called ערך סתום. The term is unclear, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: An unspecified valuation, where a person pledges a ערך without naming whose
'To include', meaning a word that adds a case

steps.title: An unspecified valuation pays the smallest amount: three shekels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that someone who pledges 'an unspecified ערך' pays the lowest valuation, which is three שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: one who says 'an unspecified valuation is on me' gives the smallest of the valuations. How much is the smallest? Three שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. A person who pledged a ערך without naming anyone pays the smallest ערך, three שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no person was named, we don't know which ערך he meant. The ruling is to pay the lowest amount the תורה lists, which is three שקלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest of the valuations
Three שקלים, the lowest ערך in the תורה
'Upon me', the words that make a pledge

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who says, "An unspecified valuation is upon me"
gives the amount of the smallest of the valuations.
And how much is the smallest of the valuations?
Three shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by defining ערך סתום and what it costs.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pledge of an unspecified ערך pays the smallest ערך, three שקלים.

steps.title: Why not fifty shekels?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges the ruling: why not say he pays fifty שקלים, the largest ערך?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say he gives fifty!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the three-שקלים ruling. It asks why we don't make him pay the highest amount instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The highest ערך is fifty שקלים, for a man aged twenty to sixty. If the pledge is unclear, one could argue it should be read in the biggest way. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...', which offers another possibility as a challenge
Fifty שקלים, the largest ערך

phrases.english: But say he should give fifty!
phrases.notes: Fifty is the highest ערך, for a man from twenty to sixty (ויקרא 27:3).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an unspecified ערך pays three שקלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no clear reason to choose the smallest amount over the largest, which is fifty.

steps.title: Grab a lot and you grab nothing; grab a little and you have it
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: when unsure, we take the smaller amount, because it is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you didn't grab. If you grabbed a little, you grabbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge with a well-known rule. When the amount is unclear, we choose the smaller one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smaller amount is included inside any larger amount, so three שקלים is owed for sure. Anything more is in doubt, so we don't demand it. Reaching for fifty would mean holding onto something we can't prove.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Grab a lot and you didn't grab': taking the bigger amount leaves you with nothing certain
'Grab a little and you grabbed': the smaller amount is certain

steps.whatToRemember: An unspecified ערך pays three שקלים, because of the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: when in doubt, take the smaller, certain amount.
steps.whyThisMatters: תפשת מרובה לא תפשת is a general rule used in many places in ש״ס to decide unclear amounts.

phrases.english: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp;
if you grasped a little, you grasped.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּפַשְׂתָּה מְרוּבֶּה לֹא תָּפַשְׂתָּה, תָּפַשְׂתָּה מוּעָט תָּפַשְׂתָּה

steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unclear pledge might be read at the highest ערך, fifty שקלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: We take the smallest amount, three שקלים, because only that is certain.

steps.title: Why not say the lowest ערך is one שקל?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges the three-שקל ruling with a פסוק that links every ערך to a single שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say he pays just one שקל, since the פסוק says: 'And every ערך of yours shall be by the holy שקל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the answer of three שקלים. It points to a פסוק that seems to make one שקל the smallest ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that when unsure, we take the smallest amount. One שקל is even smaller than three. So if the Torah mentions one שקל for ערכין, maybe that is the true 'smallest ערך.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'But let us say.' This brings in another way to read the case.
A silver coin. ערכין are measured in it.
The 'holy שקל,' the standard שקל used for the מקדש.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an unspecified ערך is three שקלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we take the smallest amount, and a פסוק links ערכין to one שקל, then one שקל should be the minimum.

steps.title: The one-שקל verse is about a poor person
steps.stepSummary: The one-שקל rule applies only to someone who cannot afford the full ערך (הֶשֵּׂג יָד). It is not a real ערך amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק was written about a person who cannot afford to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the one-שקל idea comes from the laws of a poor person. It is not one of the fixed ערך amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed ערכין go from three to fifty שקלים. One שקל is only the floor for a poor person who cannot pay his full pledge. So the smallest actual ערך is still three.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'what the hand can reach.' The payment is adjusted to what a poor person can afford.

phrases.english: That verse is about affordability
that it is written.
phrases.notes: He means a poor person who pledged a ערך but can't pay. He still has to give at least one שקל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenging verse to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one-שקל verse gives the smallest ערך.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-שקל verse is only about a poor person. The smallest real ערך is three שקלים.

steps.title: Then why do we need the פסוק at all?
steps.stepSummary: If logic alone (take the smaller amount) already gives three שקלים, the פסוק בערכך seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, why do I need the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs the word בערכך to teach the ערך סתום rule. Simple logic already gives us three שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 got three שקלים from the rule of taking the smaller amount. If logic gives the answer, a פסוק teaching the same thing looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what the פסוק adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need the פסוק?' This asks what a verse adds beyond what we already know.

phrases.english: But then, why do I need the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 13's logic to question why the verse is needed.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that ערך סתום is not reduced for a poor person
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the פסוק teaches that an unspecified ערך is not lowered by הֶשֵּׂג יָד. Even a poor person pays three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the פסוק comes to say that it is not judged by what he can afford.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains what the פסוק adds. An unspecified ערך cannot be lowered to one שקל for a poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic gives us three שקלים. The פסוק adds something new: the three are firm. Other ערכין can drop to one שקל for a poor person, but this one cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is judged.' Here: whether the amount is set by the poor-person rules.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says
that Rabba bar Avuh says:
To say that it is not judged by affordability.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִידּוֹן בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by giving the verse a new job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse teaches an extra law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse only repeats the three-שקל logic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that an unspecified ערך is never lowered for a poor person.

steps.title: Why is it not lowered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why an unspecified ערך should be treated differently from other ערכין. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other ערך can be lowered for a poor person. So the גמרא wants to know what makes this kind special.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?'

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an unspecified ערך is not subject to הֶשֵּׂג יָד.

steps.title: It is as if he named the amount
steps.stepSummary: An unspecified ערך is treated as if the person said out loud, 'I pledge three שקלים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is as if he spelled it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this pledge counts like a pledge of a stated sum of money. The poor-person rules do not apply to a stated sum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor-person reduction applies only to the ערכין that the Torah fixed for a person. Here the person in effect pledged a set amount of money. So he owes the full three שקלים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is like one who stated it clearly.' He is treated as if he named the amount.

phrases.english: It is considered as if he spelled it out.
phrases.notes: As if he said, 'I pledge three שקלים,' a set amount of money and not a person's ערך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An unspecified ערך is treated like a stated pledge of three שקלים, so it is not lowered.

steps.title: Second version: ערך סתום is lowered for a poor person
steps.stepSummary: Some report the opposite in רב נחמן's name: an unspecified ערך is subject to הֶשֵּׂג יָד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it is judged by what he can afford.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב נחמן's statement. It says the opposite of the first: a poor person may pay less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the פסוק בערכך makes the unspecified ערך just like every other ערך. A poor person can pay one שקל.
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions come from the same רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, but they reach opposite rulings. Do not mix them up: version one says the ערך is not lowered, version two says it is.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Naḥman says
that Rabba bar Avuh says:
It is judged by affordability.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: נִידּוֹן בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposite version of the answer given in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified ערך can be lowered for a poor person.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version: of course it works like every other ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why anyone needs to say this. Every ערך follows the poor-person rule, so this one should too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching that only repeats the normal rule seems to add nothing. So the גמרא asks what new point is being made.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious!' This challenges a statement that seems to add nothing new.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every ערך follows the poor-person rule, saying it here teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Without it, we might have thought it was a stated amount
steps.stepSummary: We might have treated an unspecified ערך as a stated pledge of three שקלים. The teaching tells us it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it is as if he spelled it out. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the teaching is needed. Without it, we might have used the exact reasoning of the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from step 19 ('as if he named the amount') is here the mistaken thought that the teaching rejects. In this version, an unspecified ערך is still a real ערך, so a poor person can pay less.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said.' This shows the mistaken idea the teaching comes to correct.
'It teaches us.' This shows the new point being made.

steps.whatToRemember: Version one: ערך סתום counts like a stated three שקלים, so a poor person pays all three. Version two: it is a normal ערך, so a poor person can pay less. The reason 'כִּמְפָרֵשׁ דָּמֵי' is the law in version one and the rejected idea in version two.

phrases.english: Lest you say
it is considered as if he spelled it out,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כִּמְפָרֵשׁ דָּמֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a mistaken idea the teaching comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unspecified ערך is like a stated pledge of three שקלים and cannot be lowered.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a normal ערך and can be lowered for a poor person.

steps.title: A second lesson: only the ערך of the whole person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from בערכך that a person pledges the ערך of his whole self, not the ערך of one limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'בערכך' teaches that he gives the ערך of his whole self. He does not give a ערך for the value of limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא, which gives a second lesson from the word בערכך. ערך works only for a whole person, not for one body part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ערך is a fixed Torah amount for a whole person. If someone pledges 'the ערך of my hand,' this ערך law does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another explanation.' A second lesson from the same word.
The ערך of his whole self.
The value of limbs or body parts.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
"According to your valuation":
he gives the valuation of his whole self,
and he does not give the valuation of the value of limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: בְּעֶרְכְּךָ — עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ הוּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא for a second lesson from בערכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערך applies only to a whole person, not to a single limb.

steps.title: But that word was already used for ערך סתום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בערכך can teach the limb rule when it was already used to teach ערך סתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used this word to teach about an unspecified ערך!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that one word cannot be used for two lessons. בערכך already taught the unspecified ערך rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once a word teaches one law, it is 'used up.' Step 10 already used בערכך for ערך סתום. So where does the limb lesson come from?

keyTerms.meaning: 'You have taken it out,' meaning you already used this word for another lesson.
A ערך pledged without saying whose.

phrases.english: But you have already used it
for an unspecified valuation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using בערכך for the limb rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word was already used for ערך סתום, so it cannot also teach the limb rule.

steps.title: The word holds two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written just 'ערך' but wrote 'בערכך'. The extra form gives room for two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read into it both 'ערך' and 'בערכך.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word is longer than needed. That extra wording lets it teach both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah needed only 'ערך.' Writing 'בערכך' gives extra wording to learn from. One part teaches ערך סתום and the other teaches the limb rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Read into it.' Find two readings in one word.

steps.whatToRemember: From the one word בערכך we learn two things: an unspecified ערך is valid (three שקלים), and a ערך works only for a whole person, not for a limb.

phrases.english: Read into it
"Valuation" and "according to your valuation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows two lessons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word can only teach one lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: בערכך is longer than 'ערך,' so it teaches both ערך סתום and the whole-person rule.

steps.title: A part that life depends on counts as the whole person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches from נפשות that pledging the ערך of a body part that life depends on obligates the full ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that I also leave out a body part that life depends on. So the verse says 'נפשות' (persons).
steps.whatsHappening: We just learned that pledging the ערך of one limb means nothing. Now the ברייתא says a part that life depends on is different. The word נפשות teaches that pledging it counts as pledging the whole person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this verse, we would treat a head or heart like any other limb, so the pledge would mean nothing. נפשות is connected to נפש, life itself. So a part that holds a person's life is treated as the person, and he must pay his full ערך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think': it opens a possible mistaken idea that the verse then corrects
Soul, life
A body part that a person's life depends on
'Persons' (plural of נפש), the word in the ערכין verse

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the limb rule from בערכך. An ordinary limb still means nothing. Only a part that life depends on counts as the whole person.

phrases.english: One might think that I exclude
even a part on which life depends,
the verse teaches: 'Persons,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 23 that a pledge of one limb means nothing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pledging the ערך of a part that life depends on obligates the full ערך of the person.

steps.title: The dead have no ערך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns a second lesson from נפשות: a dead person cannot be pledged as an ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Persons': this means living people, and not the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the same word נפשות to teach that the laws of ערכין apply only to living people. A מת has no ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נפש means a living being, and a dead body no longer has one. So a pledge of a מת's ערך obligates nothing. This is a second lesson from the same word, which sets up the גמרא's question next.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person

phrases.english: 'Persons' — and not the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second lesson drawn from the same word used in step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead person cannot be pledged as an ערך.

steps.title: The word was already used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that נפשות was already used for the rule about a part that life depends on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used this word for something else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. One word cannot normally be used for two separate lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 used נפשות to teach the rule about a part that life depends on. Step 27 uses the same word to leave out the dead. The question is where the second lesson comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You already used it up', meaning this word was already used for a different lesson

phrases.english: But you already used it [for another teaching]!
phrases.notes: He means the lesson from step 26, about a part that life depends on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double use of נפשות in steps 26 and 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of נפשות to leave out the dead
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word was already used for the rule about a part that life depends on, so it is not free to teach anything else.

steps.title: The plural form gives two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written נפש but wrote נפשות, so the word carries two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'נפש' and 'נפשות': the singular alone would have been enough, so the plural adds an extra lesson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word holds two lessons. The basic form נפש teaches one thing, and the extra plural form teaches another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 25, where 'בערכך' instead of 'ערך' gave room for two lessons. Here 'נפשות' instead of 'נפש' does the same. So both the rule about a part that life depends on and the rule about the dead can come from this one word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Read into it': read the word as if it holds more than one form
'Person', the singular form the Torah could have used

phrases.english: Read into it 'person' and 'persons.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נפשות can teach only one lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural form beyond the needed singular gives room for two lessons.

steps.title: A dying person (גוסס) is also left out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'והעמיד והעריך' that a גוסס cannot be pledged as an ערך either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should I leave out only the dead, and not a person who is dying? So the verse says 'he shall be stood up and valued.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether a person who is still alive but dying can be pledged. It answers no, from the verse about standing the person before the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוסס is still alive, so you might think he is included. But the verse says the person is stood before the כהן and then valued. Only someone who can be stood up can be valued, and a גוסס cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on his deathbed, still alive but close to death
'He shall be stood up and valued', the verse that links standing before the כהן with being valued

phrases.english: Should I exclude the dead,
but not exclude the dying person?
The verse teaches: 'He shall be stood up and valued.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8. Only someone who can be stood before the כהן can be valued.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמֵּת, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַגּוֹסֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule about the dead from step 27 to someone who is dying
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוסס cannot be pledged as an ערך, because he cannot be stood before the כהן.

steps.title: The same verse could leave out the dead too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need נפשות for the dead, since 'והעמיד והעריך' already leaves them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, I could learn that the dead are left out from 'he shall be stood up and valued' as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If standing before the כהן is required, a dead person obviously fails that test too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead person can't be stood up any more than a גוסס can. So the verse from step 30 already covers the dead. That makes the use of נפשות for the dead in step 27 look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': it opens a challenge that follows from what was just said
'Let me learn it' from a different source

phrases.english: If so,
let me also learn that the dead [are left out]
from 'he shall be stood up and valued'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מֵת נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִ״וְּהֶעֱמִיד וְהֶעֱרִיךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 30 to challenge step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of נפשות to leave out the dead (step 27)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'והעמיד והעריך' already leaves out anyone who cannot stand, and a dead person cannot stand.

steps.title: Yes, the dead are learned from that verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the rule about the dead does come from 'והעמיד והעריך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, that is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. The rule about the dead really is learned from the verse about standing before the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending נפשות as the source for the dead, the גמרא agrees with the question. But that leaves נפשות without a job, and the next step picks up exactly that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Indeed, that is so': the גמרא accepts the point that was raised

phrases.english: Indeed, so it is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in step 31
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dead are left out because of נפשות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dead are left out because of 'והעמיד והעריך'.

steps.title: Then what is נפש / נפשות for?
steps.stepSummary: Since the dead are learned from another verse, the גמרא asks what the extra plural form teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need 'נפש' and 'נפשות'?
steps.whatsHappening: Having agreed in step 32, the גמרא now asks what the extra plural form is for. The Torah does not add extra wording for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 29 the plural form was supposed to give a second lesson, the one about the dead. Now the dead come from 'והעמיד והעריך'. So the extra plural form seems to have no job left.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need it?': a question about a word or teaching that seems unnecessary

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'person' and 'persons'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from accepting the challenge in step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra lesson from the plural form נפשות (step 29)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the dead are learned from 'והעמיד והעריך', the extra plural form has nothing left to teach.

steps.title: It teaches a lesson coming up soon
steps.stepSummary: The extra form נפשות is used for a different lesson, which the גמרא will give shortly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what we are about to say below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plural form teaches some other rule. It does not say what that rule is yet and points ahead to the coming discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra wording is not wasted. It is simply needed for a different lesson than the dead. The גמרא will explain that lesson in the lines that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we are going to say'
'Below' or 'soon': later in the discussion

steps.whatToRemember: The rule about a part that life depends on comes from נפשות. The rule that the dead and the dying are left out comes from 'והעמיד והעריך': only someone who can be stood before the כהן can be valued. The extra plural form is saved for including a מנוול and a מוכה שחין, as step 39 explains.

phrases.english: As we are about to say below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points the word to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra plural form has no job left.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra plural form teaches a different rule: including a מנוול and a מוכה שחין (step 39).

steps.title: One person can pledge the value of a hundred people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives another reading of נפשות: one person can make an ערך pledge for many people at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of 'persons': I would only know that one person can pledge the ערך of one person. How do we know one person can pledge the ערך of a hundred? The verse says 'persons'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes another lesson from the plural word נפשות. The lesson is that one person can pledge the ערך of many people at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the plural, we might think an ערך pledge works only one person for one person. The plural 'persons' shows that a single person can pledge the ערכין of many people. This is the first of several lessons the ברייתא draws from נפשות. The one step 34 pointed to is the מנוול and מוכה שחין lesson (steps 37 and 39).

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a different reading of the same word
'Persons', the plural word in the פסוק of ערכין
He pledged someone's fixed Torah value (ערך) to the הקדש
From where do we know this?
The verse comes to teach; this introduces the source

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'persons'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד,
phrases.english: I would only know of one who pledged the value of one;
one who pledged the value of a hundred, from where do we know?
The verse teaches: 'persons'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר, נְפָשֹׁת — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's list of lessons from נפשות. This list leads to the lesson step 34 pointed to, the מנוול and מוכה שחין in steps 37–39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person may pledge the ערכין of many people, learned from the plural נפשות.

steps.title: A woman can also pledge an ערך
steps.stepSummary: Another reading of נפשות: women, and not only men, can make an ערך pledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of 'persons': I would only know that a man can pledge the ערך of a man or of a woman. How do we know that a woman can pledge the ערך of a man or of a woman? The verse says 'persons'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives another lesson from נפשות. A woman can also make an ערך pledge, whether for a man or for a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section begins with the word 'man' (איש), so we might think only men can make this pledge. The plural 'persons' widens the rule to include a woman as the one making the pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: A man; the opening word of the ערכין section
A woman
She pledged someone's ערך
Whether... or...

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'persons'
I would only know of a man who pledged a value,
whether of a man or of a woman;
a woman who pledged the value of a man,
and a woman who pledged the value of a woman, from where do we know?
The verse teaches: 'persons'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר, נְפָשֹׁת — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second lesson from the same word נפשות, listed in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may pledge an ערך, for either a man or a woman.

steps.title: Including a repulsive person and one covered in boils
steps.stepSummary: A third reading of נפשות: we can pledge the ערך of a מנוול or a מוכה שחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of 'persons': it comes to include a repulsive-looking person and a person covered in boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third lesson from נפשות. The ערך of a מנוול or a מוכה שחין can be pledged too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This lesson is about whose ערך can be pledged, not about who makes the pledge. It sets up the next question, because now one word seems to be teaching three different things.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to bring in a case we might have left out
A repulsive-looking or disfigured person
A person covered in boils

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'persons'
comes to include a repulsive person and one covered in boils.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: נְפָשֹׁת — לְהָבִיא מְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third lesson from the same word, which leads straight into the next question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערך of a מנוול or a מוכה שחין can be pledged.

steps.title: The word was already used for the other lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: נפשות was already used for the hundred people and for the woman, so how can it also teach about the מנוול?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used this word to teach those other cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The word נפשות was already used up on the earlier lessons, so it cannot also teach the מנוול and the מוכה שחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one extra word teaches one lesson. The ברייתא seems to squeeze three lessons out of the same word, so the גמרא asks how that can work.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, surely; opens an objection
You already used it (literally, 'you took it out') for another lesson
Those (earlier cases)

phrases.english: But you already used it for those!
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the earlier lessons: one person pledging for a hundred, and a woman pledging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 37 for using a word already taken by steps 35-36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of נפשות to include מנוול and מוכה שחין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One extra word cannot teach several separate lessons; it was already used for the hundred people and for the woman.

steps.title: The other lessons do not need the extra word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earlier lessons are equal to each other and all come together without the plural. The plural is really needed only for the מנוול and the מוכה שחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those cases do not need a verse. Why? Because they are all equal, so they all come in together. Where the verse was truly needed, it was needed for the repulsive person and the one covered in boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The earlier lessons are equally strong and come from the basic wording on their own. The extra plural is saved for the מנוול and the מוכה שחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no one of the earlier lessons is stronger than the others, there is no reason to pick one over another, so they all come in together without the extra plural. That leaves the plural נפשות free to teach just one real lesson, the מנוול and the מוכה שחין. So the word is not doing triple duty after all.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא's other lessons are wrong. They still stand. The גמרא is only saying they don't need the extra plural.

steps.title: The verse includes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס in pledges of value
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'והיה ערכך' that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are included in pledges of דמים, even though they have no ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'And your valuation shall be' come to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס in pledges of value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the ברייתא's line about והיה ערכך, which was quoted earlier (step 5), so it can examine it. That line says a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס can be the subject of a pledge of their market value (דמים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not in ערכין, because the תורה's fixed amounts are given only for a clear male or female. Still, the ברייתא says the פסוק includes them for a pledge of דמים, meaning their actual market value. The גמרא will now ask why we need a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose sex cannot be determined
A person with both male and female features
Market value, what a person would sell for (unlike ערך, which is a fixed amount set by the תורה)
To include

phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:3

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are included in pledges of דמים.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed for value pledges?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed. Anyone who pledges the value of something, even a palm tree, must pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק for value pledges? Treat it like the value of a palm tree. If someone said 'the value of a palm tree is upon me,' wouldn't he have to pay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. A pledge of value works for any object, so why does the תורה need a special פסוק for a טומטום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pledge of דמים is simply a promise to give the worth of something. That works for a tree, so it surely works for a person. A פסוק to teach this seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק? (asking why something obvious needs a source)
A palm tree
Wouldn't he give? (a question meaning: of course he would)

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for pledges of value?
Let it be no different from the value of a palm tree.
If he had said, "The value of this palm tree [is upon me],"
would he not have to give it?

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'והיה ערכך' to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס in דמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pledges of value work for anything, even a tree, so the פסוק teaches nothing new.

steps.title: רבא: the verse teaches that they are judged by the importance of the body part
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק teaches נידון בכבודו. If they pledge the value of a vital part, they pay for the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק comes to teach that he is judged by the importance of the part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what the פסוק adds. Even for a טומטום, a pledge of a vital body part counts as a pledge of the whole person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a pledge for the value of a tree's branch would cost only the branch's value. With a person, pledging the value of a part he cannot live without, like his head, counts as pledging his whole value. The פסוק teaches that this rule applies to a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס too.

keyTerms.meaning: Judged by its importance: pledging a vital body part means paying for the whole person

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the פסוק is not about whether a value pledge works at all. It is about how much the person must pay.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It comes to say that he is judged by its importance.
phrases.notes: If they pledge the value of a part they can't live without, like the head, they pay the value of the whole body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the פסוק is teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to teach only that a value pledge works, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches נידון בכבודו: a vital part counts as the whole body, even for a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: Why we might have thought otherwise
steps.stepSummary: Without the פסוק, we might have tied נידון בכבודו to ערכין. Then only people who are in ערכין would follow this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the פסוק says 'a vow by your valuation,' anyone in ערכין is judged by the importance of the part, and anyone not in ערכין is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by showing the mistake we would have made without the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נדר בערכך' link vows of value with ערכין. From that link we might have said that only someone who has an ערך is judged by the importance of the part. So a טומטום would pay only the value of the part itself. The extra פסוק tells us that is wrong.

phrases.english: and whoever is not included in valuations is not judged by its importance.

steps.terutzMaskana: Even those outside ערכין, like a טומטום, are judged by the importance of the part.

steps.title: אביי questions whether someone outside ערכין is judged by importance
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא whether someone who is not in ערכין really can be judged by the importance of the part.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is one who is not in ערכין judged by the importance of the part?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a challenge to רבא. The next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that the rule of נידון בכבודו could apply outside ערכין, and that the פסוק only had to teach it. אביי questions that very assumption. In his view, outside ערכין there is no such rule at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And one who is not included in ערכין

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outside ערכין, a pledge of a vital part does not seem to bring in the whole value.

steps.title: אביי's challenge: the head of a slave or a donkey
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא. Consecrating or selling the head of a slave or donkey only makes a partnership. It does not hand over the whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'The head of this slave is הקדש': he and הקדש are partners in it. 'The head of the slave is sold to you': they appraise it and split. The same applies to a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his challenge from a ברייתא. In these cases, giving away the head does not count as giving away the whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are about property, not ערכין. The head is the most vital part, yet the owner does not have to give the whole slave or donkey. He only becomes a partner. So outside ערכין we do not see נידון בכבודו, which goes against רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
Partners

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'partners' does not mean the whole slave or donkey goes to הקדש or to the buyer. Each side owns a share, and that is exactly why this is a problem for רבא.

steps.title: The cow's head is sold or consecrated by itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Selling or consecrating a cow's head covers only the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'The head of this cow is sold to you,' he sold only the head. Even more: if he says 'The head of this cow is הקדש,' only the head belongs to הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading אביי's ברייתא. With a cow, the head alone is sold or consecrated, and the rest of the cow is not affected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slave or donkey, saying 'the head' makes a partnership in the whole animal. With a cow, only the head itself is transferred. Either way, the whole animal is not judged by its vital part.

steps.title: Why a cow's head is different
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a cow's head counts by itself because it is sold separately at the butcher.

steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains why a cow's head is treated as its own item, unlike a slave's or donkey's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People normally buy and sell a cow's head by itself at the butcher, so it is a separate item. A slave's or donkey's head is never sold by itself. Saying 'the head' there can only mean a share in the whole.

steps.stepSummary: אביי draws his point from the ברייתא. A donkey and a cow are not in ערכין, and they are not judged by the vital part.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a donkey and a cow are not in ערכין, and they are not judged by their important part!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge to רבא. The ברייתא shows that animals, which are not in ערכין, do not follow נידון בכבודו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had said the פסוק teaches נידון בכבודו even for things outside ערכין. Yet in the ברייתא, consecrating an animal's head does not consecrate the whole animal. This suggests that נידון בכבודו belongs only to ערכין.

steps.title: A slave is in ערכין, yet he is not judged by the vital part either
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back. By אביי's logic, the slave in the ברייתא should be a problem too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, a slave should be a problem for you: he is in ערכין, and yet he is not judged by his importance!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא turns אביי's argument around. The same ברייתא treats a slave the same way, even though a slave is in ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ערכין were the reason, a slave should be judged by the vital part. But the ברייתא says consecrating a slave's head only makes a partnership. So ערכין cannot be the real dividing line, and אביי's proof falls apart.

steps.title: Altar holiness versus Temple-maintenance holiness
steps.stepSummary: The real split is the type of הקדש. The ברייתא speaks of קדשי מזבח, while נידון בכבודו applies to קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this is about things consecrated for the altar, and that is about things consecrated for Temple upkeep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash with a new dividing line. It is not ערכין versus not ערכין. It is which kind of הקדש is involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of the slave and donkey speaks of קדשי מזבח, where the whole is not judged by its part. The rule of paying the whole value for a vital part applies to קדשי בדק הבית. Money from ערכין also goes to בדק הבית.

steps.whatToRemember: נידון בכבודו depends on the kind of הקדש, not on whether something is in ערכין. It applies to בדק הבית.

steps.title: For the altar, holiness should spread to the whole cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קדשי מזבח reading from the end of the ברייתא. With altar holiness, a consecrated head should make the whole cow holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the ברייתא, as קדשי מזבח? Then look at the end: 'Even if he says the head of this cow is הקדש, only its head belongs to הקדש.' Why? Let the holiness spread through the whole cow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If the ברייתא is about altar holiness, the ending about the cow does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending says only the cow's head becomes הקדש. With קדשי מזבח, holiness placed on part of an animal should spread to all of it. So the ending seems to clash with the קדשי מזבח reading.
